headline: MP Rumeen Farhana subjected to abusive language in Parliament
summary: The Brahmanbaria-2 independent MP alleged that fellow lawmakers used abusive language against her, calling it a violation of parliamentary norms.
details: Brahmanbaria-2 independent MP Rumeen Farhana has alleged that she was subjected to abusive language by fellow lawmakers during a parliamentary session yesterday.
The incident occurred while she was speaking on the Bank Resolution (Amendment) Bill, during which ruling party MPs created an uproar.
Rumeen stated that the behavior she witnessed is not what one would expect in the parliament of a democratic country and does not fall within parliamentary norms.
She argued that if there were counter-arguments to her statements, they should have been delivered through proper parliamentary procedures rather than abusive language.
Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad responded by gesturing to stop the commotion and stating that he stands for freedom of speech in the parliament.
The Speaker urged lawmakers from both the ruling and opposition parties not to obstruct their counterparts while they are speaking.
Rumeen also referenced the 2018 parliament, noting that she faced a similarly disgraceful situation when speaking for the BNP in the Awami League-led parliament.
She expressed concern that if there is no minimum change in behavior after a change in government, there is little point in the opposition's presence in the House.
caption:
No dissenting voice can be raised? MP Rumeen Farhana alleges she was targeted with abusive language in Parliament.

The Speaker urged lawmakers from both the ruling and opposition parties not to obstruct their counterparts while they are speaking.

headline_marked: Parliament [[passes law to replace RAB with SRB]], opposition slams move
headline: Parliament passes law to replace RAB with SRB, opposition slams move
summary: The government has abolished the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and established the Special Response Battalion (SRB), though critics call it 'old wine in a new bottle'.
details: The government has passed the Special Response Battalion (SRB) Bill 2026 in parliament by voice vote, officially abolishing the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and establishing a new specialised police unit.
The move comes after years of widespread criticism of RAB, which is currently under US sanctions due to serious human rights violations, including enforced disappearances.

Opposition members, including Leader of the Opposition Shafiqur Rahman and Jamaat MP Nurul Islam, strongly objected to the bill, arguing that the SRB is effectively just RAB reorganised under a new name.
Critics claim the SRB mirrors RAB in its structure, personnel, and logistics, with Section 27 of the bill allowing the transfer of RAB's assets, powers, and records to the new unit.
Jamaat MP Nazibur Rahman noted that the UN, Human Rights Watch, and the Commission on Enforced Disappearances had all previously called for the complete dissolution of RAB.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed defended the bill, stating that it fulfills a promise to abolish RAB and that state resources, including weapons and intelligence gear, must be preserved by transferring them to the new organization.
The Home Minister also explained that a grievance redress committee will be established to handle internal complaints against members of the new unit.
caption:
RAB is gone, but is it really? Parliament has passed a law to replace it with the SRB, but the opposition calls it 'old wine in a new bottle'.

The government has passed the Special Response Battalion (SRB) Bill 2026 in parliament by voice vote, officially abolishing the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and establishing a new specialised police unit.

The move comes after years of widespread criticism of RAB, which is currently under US sanctions due to serious human rights violations, including enforced disappearances.

Opposition members, including Leader of the Opposition Shafiqur Rahman and Jamaat MP Nurul Islam, strongly objected to the bill, arguing that the SRB is effectively just RAB reorganised under a new name.

Critics claim the SRB mirrors RAB in its structure, personnel, and logistics, with Section 27 of the bill allowing the transfer of RAB's assets, powers, and records to the new unit.

Jamaat MP Nazibur Rahman noted that the UN, Human Rights Watch, and the Commission on Enforced Disappearances had all previously called for the complete dissolution of RAB.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed defended the bill, stating that it fulfills a promise to abolish RAB and that state resources, including weapons and intelligence gear, must be preserved by transferring them to the new organization.

The Home Minister also explained that a grievance redress committee will be established to handle internal complaints against members of the new unit.
